title: Count Slices That Sum to K
statement:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, return how many contiguous, non-empty slices of nums add up to exactly k.

Slices at different positions count separately, even if they hold the same values. The array can contain negative numbers and zeros.

examples.why: [2] at the start, [2, -1, 1], [-1, 1, 2] and [2] at the end. Because of the -1, a sum can go down as a slice grows, so a sliding window cannot decide when to shrink.
Every one of the 3 + 2 + 1 slices sums to 0.
[3] at index 0, [3] at index 2, and the whole array, where -3 cancels the first 3.

hints: The sum of slice [i, j] can be written with two running totals. Which two?
Let prefix[j] be the sum of the first j elements. The slice from i to j − 1 sums to k exactly when prefix[i] = prefix[j] − k.
Walk once, keeping a running sum and a map from each prefix sum seen so far to how many times it was seen. At each step add map[sum − k] to the answer. Start the map with {0: 1}.

explain.intuition:
A slice sum is a difference of two running totals: sum(i..j) = prefix[j+1] − prefix[i]. So "slices ending here that sum to k" means "earlier running totals equal to current − k". Counting those is a hash-map lookup.

A sliding window does not work here: with negatives, adding an element can make the sum smaller, so there is no rule for when to shrink. The prefix-sum map does not care about signs. The {0: 1} entry stands for the empty prefix, which lets slices that start at index 0 be counted.
steps: Add seen[sum − k] (0 if missing) to count: each earlier prefix with that total starts one slice that ends here and sums to k.
Then increase seen[sum] by 1. Doing this after the lookup keeps empty slices out when k = 0.
pitfalls: Forgetting the initial {0: 1}: slices that start at index 0 are never counted.
Updating seen[sum] before the lookup: with k = 0 every position would count an empty slice.
Using a set instead of counts: in [0, 0, 0] the same prefix total appears four times and each one starts a different slice.

solutions.title: Every start, running sum
solutions.idea: Fix a start index and extend to the right, keeping the sum as you go. Every slice is checked once.

solutions.title: Prefix sums with a count map
solutions.idea: For each running total, count how many earlier running totals are exactly k smaller.

followups: All numbers are positive. Can you solve it with O(1) extra memory?
Return the length of the longest slice that sums to k. What do you store in the map instead of a count?
